ai.description: This small frog reaches 30–40 mm. It features a bright golden-yellow dorsum, contrasting dark brown lateral bands, and long, slender limbs with expanded toe discs. It lacks a dorsolateral fold.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Hylarana aurantiaca* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, continuous, bright golden-yellow dorsolateral stripe that contrasts sharply against its reddish-brown body.
ai.habitat: Hylarana aurantiaca inhabits moist evergreen and semi-evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found near streams at elevations between 500 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: Boulenger's golden-backed frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining active at night to hunt small insects among the leaf litter and vegetation of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Hylarana aurantiaca* breeds during the monsoon, laying clutches of 100–300 eggs in gelatinous masses attached to submerged vegetation in forest streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: Boulenger's Golden-backed Frog is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu at elevations of 500–1,200 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Hylarana aurantiaca* consists of a series of short, high-pitched, insect-like chirps typically heard near streams in evergreen forests.
